title: A Little Bird Riding on an Elephant's Back
paragraphs: Hmm, where was that again? Oh, I think that was the name of Takt’s little pig sister.
“Was she Takt’s sister?”

“Yes. She seemed to resent being designated an enemy of the world, so she broke out of her hiding place and was running amok. I ran into her there, and after a head-on battle, I managed to subdue her. Here are the details…”
As he says this, Zou hands over a scroll. Since Father in this loop isn’t very good at reading or writing yet, he’s having someone nearby read it aloud to him.

To summarize the situation briefly: Takt’s little pig of a sister broke out of her hideout, used violence to punish those who spoke ill of Takt, and was running amok when this Zou came across her, leading to a fight. It seems he managed to capture her, but he let the others—except for the little pig—escape. However, when the Little Sister Pig called out to her comrades for help, Takt’s remnants reportedly spat, “That’s what happens when you get too big for your britches just because you’re Big Sister,” and abandoned her.
“So basically, they used Takt’s sister as bait to escape?”
“It appears so.”
Just hearing about it makes me want to vomit.

Then, Zou—who, like Panda, had been working as a semi-mercenary—took the Pig Sister to Faubrey for the bounty. Apparently, he was suddenly honored in his home country of Siltvelt for the feat of capturing such a big fish. The reason given was something about him being a knight in name only.

Word has it that Takt’s sister was taken to the Pig King’s harem to be used as a source of information. Apparently, the hideout she revealed was already completely empty. It seems no important information has come to light so far.
“I see… Congratulations.”
Father praised him as if he were fully convinced. Following that, a representative of the Shusaku clan and an elder of the Genmu clan stepped forward and declared:

“Our nation, Siltvelt, highly values the achievement of capturing the enemy of the world—the Takt faction—and Takt’s relatives who had been in hiding. Therefore, we appoint Elmero-Puhant as the Guardian Knight of the Shield Hero.”
“Whaaaat!?”

At this point, Father let out a cry while making a blatantly displeased face. Being a Guardian Knight means—just like Panda—she’ll be under Father’s command. Isn’t it enough just to receive words of praise from Father, the Shield Hero?
“Wait a minute. Why!?”

“A reward for her achievements is absolutely essential. Besides, she’s a former Free Knight with strength and a broad-mindedness rivaling Rasazusa’s. I believe it would be too much of a burden to have only Rasazusa as the Shield Hero’s Guardian Knight.”
“Even so…”
When Father turns his gaze toward Zou, the Zou therianthrope—who seems quite nervous—is fidgeting with his hands clasped together. For such a big guy, his reaction is rather subdued.
“What are you so shy about? Where’s your usual feistiness?”
“S-shut up! I-I’m sorry!”
In response to Panda’s provocation, Zou is arguing back while correcting himself. Ah, so he’s just winging it. It’s inconvenient when you know people, isn’t it?
“Well… I do think it’s a burden to have Ms. Larsa be my bodyguard all the time, but Motoyasu-kun and Sakura-chan are here too…”

“I understand that the Spear Hero and his Filolial followers are here. However, it’s also a fact that Siltvelt must take the lead in protecting you… For the sake of boosting morale, I’d be grateful if you could accept this.”
Hearing this, Father let out another sigh.

“…All right. I was planning to have Larsa look into various things anyway, and considering what lies ahead, it’s better to have more people on hand. But an elephant, huh… I have this memory of nearly being attacked by a mammoth in the bath…”
“Ah, she’s probably my cousin. I apologize for having such an unrestrained relative…”
Zou said, as if the words were being squeezed out of him. Is Zou a relative of the mammoth? The races of Siltvelt are so diverse that I’m not entirely sure, but I suppose that’s just how it is.
“Ah, yeah… I don’t mind… Just don’t expect too much from me. You seem a little anxious about your position—are you okay?”
“Yes. It’s been determined that you’ve established a track record worthy of this role.”
“Oh, I see. If you’re aware of that, then fine.”
With a tone that sounded almost resigned, Father sat back slightly in his throne, looking as though his motivation had waned. Zou, on the other hand, took on an expression brimming with enthusiasm.
“Yes! I look forward to working with you from now on. I, Elmero! I intend to stake my life on protecting the Shield Hero!”
“Ho ho ho, just don’t put too much pressure on yourself. Just like Rasazusa, you just need to protect the Shield Hero naturally.”

The old man of the Genmu clan cautioned Zou. This… it seems I’m gradually getting a sense of Father’s type. I sense Attributes in Zou that are somewhat similar to Panda’s. It’s a strategy to win over Father that’s different from both Panda’s and the Older Sister. I remember a Rival doing something similarly underhanded a long time ago.
“Nice to meet you.”
Father’s dry reply left quite an impression.
“Wow, you’re huge! You’re even bigger than Sakura!”
Sakura-chan cheerfully approaches Zou.
“I look forward to getting to know you.”
“Nice to meet you!”
When Sakura-chan greets him, Zou smiles gently.
“Want a piggyback ride?”
“Huh? What?”
“Like this.”
Saying that, the elephant crouched down, scooped up Sakura-chan, and, using its trunk deftly, placed her on its head. Sakura-chan broke into a smile, probably enjoying the higher vantage point.
“Whoa, I’m so high up!”
Sakura-chan placed her hands on the elephant’s head and looked out at the surroundings.
“It’s totally different from jumping!”
“That looks so fun! Let Kou ride, too!”
“Sure. Go ahead.”
And just like that, Sakura-chan and Kou started getting excited. Oh, look—the elephant is carrying Sakura-chan and Kou at the same time. That’s heavier than a panda.
Hmm… this is a fine elephant. I’ll bump up its rating a little.
“That’s so improper!”
Yuki-chan calls out to them, but Sakura-chan and the others aren’t listening at all. Well, I suppose it’s not really Yuki-chan’s style.
“I wonder if he likes kids?”
“I don’t know about that. Isn’t he just trying to score some points?”
Perhaps oblivious to the panda’s snide remark, the elephant carried Sakura and the others on his back and walked around the throne room for a while.
“A little bird riding on an elephant’s back… just kidding,”
Father muttered—a remark that really stuck with me.
A little while later, the Dragon Emperor’s Core Stone I’d requested was brought in from the treasury.
“…Huh? Was it like this?”
Father examined the shattered Core Stone, which had been extracted from the Takt Dragon I’d defeated.
“Is it different?”
“Yeah. I remember what it looked like when we extracted it, so I can tell—it’s shattered differently. Doesn’t the color seem a little off, too?”

Upon hearing that, I’ll check the dragon’s core stone. It looks like nothing more than a pile of shattered crystal shards. But… I’ll use a high-precision appraisal to verify the Dragon Emperor’s core stone.
Imitation Dragon Heart
After the name “Dragon Emperor’s Core Stone” flashed briefly, it changed.
“It’s a fake!”
“What!?”
“What!?”

When I announced this, everyone nearby swarmed around the Core Stone and began examining it. Then, a thorough search of the treasury began. Apparently, there were faint traces left behind by an intruder who used advanced stealth techniques. It’s believed the crime likely took place around the time we went to Shieldfreeden.
“Surely not… did thieves actually slip through these security measures and break in!?”

The people of Siltvelt all let out cries of astonishment. Since Siltvelt is a nation of Demi-Humans and Therianthropes, security at the treasury is extremely tight. The fact that the crime was committed while some could still sniff out the location of even those in stealth sent a chill down our spines.
“Even with the Filolials Motoyasu-kun raised standing by in the castle, they still didn’t notice…”
Among the people I know, there are only a handful who possess such skill.

First and foremost is my older sister. She’s always been a master of illusion magic, and I’ve heard she held a significant advantage even against the Fox of Takt. Next are the creatures Father created based on my older sister, whom he cherished so dearly. They’re technical experts just like my older sister.
Next would be… my older sister’s late friend. That one was also incredibly skilled at hiding, which is why Lord Filolial couldn’t detect him. However, in this loop, he should already be dead.
Could it be that my older sister… has joined the Takt faction or something!?

No… let’s think this through calmly. Stay cool. What if my Older Sister, who came to pick me up, is simply testing me now that I’ve restarted the loop? She’s testing whether I can handle a loop journey with Filo-tan using dragons.

But… if that were the case, I feel like she’d have warned me beforehand. I don’t think my Older Sister would go about things in such a roundabout way. If anything, I’d rather she just brought Filo-chan here. I just can’t understand why she’s making me loop again.
Anyone else…?
“Hey, Motoyasu-kun, given how specific this is, I think there’s a possibility the Takt faction is involved. Do you have any idea who might be capable of this?”
“Well, the Fox has already been taken care of…”
If he were still alive, he’d be the first person I’d suspect, but in this world, he’s already been dealt with. As for anyone else… it’s just a motley crew.
“With so few clues, it’s highly likely the culprit is someone who’s received proper training. Perhaps someone from a nation’s covert operations unit…”
“Come to think of it… I seem to recall that among the pigs executed in the first world, there was a guy who belonged to the Shadow Division of Faubrey?”
Perhaps my words struck a chord, because Father and the others from Siltvelt all looked convinced. Am I on the right track?
“I see… If there’s a high-level Shadow involved, it’s not impossible.”
“If the goal were assassination or planting dangerous items or poisons, we’d be able to detect it, but while the Shield Heroes are away… Ugh… My apologies, Heroes!”
“You’ve got to know there’s a limit to how lax your security can be! Assign people who can uncover these cover-ups more effectively.”
Because of you lot, the ‘Filo-chan Eternal’ plan is on the verge of falling apart. Shieldfreeden and Siltvelt are cut from the same cloth! You’re nothing but a bunch of incompetents.
“No… don’t worry about it. I thought they’d be targeting us, but seeing them pull a stunt like this makes it clear we need to deploy the dragons even sooner.”

Father muttered, as if he’d grasped the gravity of the situation. It certainly feels like we’re falling behind in various ways. It feels like he’s come to understand firsthand just how troublesome these hidden terrorists are.
“Does that mean they also want to retrieve the Dragon Emperor and seize real power in Shieldfreeden?”
“No, Shieldfreeden is already practically a vassal state of Siltvelt, so even if they brought in dragons from outside, it wouldn’t make any difference.”
“Is that so?”

“Yeah. It’s strange that the Takt faction would go to such lengths to flaunt a dragon like that. It’s basically them proving they’re part of the Takt faction. Of course, it might make it easier for them to lie low.”
So that means there must be another reason. Knowing Takt, it’s quite possible he’s been discussing all sorts of things with those pigs.
“That seems likely… Well, In a few months or so, the seal on the Spirit Tortoise is supposed to be broken.”
“The Spirit Tortoise?”

“That’s right. It’s said to be a powerful guardian beast—a monster that gathers the souls of living creatures to create a barrier that protects the world from the Waves. Because of it, nearly… about two-thirds of the world’s population was once sacrificed.”
“Two-thirds… that’s an extraordinary number…”
Indeed. Ultimately, protecting the world came at the cost of that many lives. These are the very ones who caused us trouble in the next loop of this cycle.
“So there are creatures like that, too. I get that, but… what does that have to do with this?”

“There are four types of guardian beasts in total: the Spirit Tortoise, the Phoenix, the Qilin, and the Dragon King… Takt’s dragon is connected to the seal of the Dragon King, and it can actually become the Dragon King!”
“What!? So you’re saying the stolen Dragon Emperor’s Core Stone will unleash the Dragon King?”
“Good heavens…”
Almost everyone present has turned pale. Well, I suppose it’s a good thing they’ve come to realize just how troublesome the Dragon King is.

“The remnants of the Takt faction possess a Core Stone with that much power… They can take revenge on the Heroes and conquer the world by force at the same time. To think such a means lies within something like that…”
“This is a real headache… Should we start getting ready to flee?”
“Lasa!”
Zou is scolding Panda. Since Panda is a mercenary, he always seems so carefree.
“Guardian Knight Lasa Zusa! Be mindful of your position!”
“I know, but isn’t it okay to say something like that?　The world doesn’t run on charity alone, and as a leader, shouldn’t you be thinking about the people?”
“Guh…!”
“Calm down. Lasa isn’t serious. He’s just saying we should probably start preparing to evacuate.”
“It’s a bit embarrassing to be overestimated like that, though. It just means that if I were a mercenary, I’d already be thinking about pulling out.”
“It’s certainly important to keep evacuation in mind. But the people here are all tough guys. Isn’t that what we’re here for—to overcome difficulties?”

Panda and Zou have different opinions, don’t they? I guess that just shows there are differences even among former mercenaries. Personally, I agree with Zou’s opinion. If the Dragon King shows up alone, it’s game over.
“Use the full might of our nation to capture that thief! And since this issue has long since surpassed the scope of a single country, report it to Faubrey immediately!”
